key_insight: Fine-tuned MACE potentials predict that MgSiO₃ post-perovskite conducts 44–55% more lattice heat than bridgmanite at equal pressure and temperature.
engineering_relevance: This computational geoscience study—not solar-cell research—provides thermal-conductivity inputs for lower-mantle and core–mantle boundary heat-flow models.
method: Fine-tune phase-specific MACE potentials for MgO, bridgmanite, and post-perovskite.
Replace DFT force evaluations in linearized phonon Boltzmann transport calculations.
Combine phase-boundary calculations with aggregate conductivity bounds.
evidence_signal: For MgO at 0 GPa, replacing MACE forces with DFT forces changes predicted conductivity by only 0.2% at 300 K and 1.9% at 2000 K.
watch_item: The reported core–mantle boundary aggregate bounds of 9.5–11.4 W/(m K) assume an Fe-free mixture of 80 vol% silicate and 20 vol% MgO, limiting direct application to chemically complex mantle materials.
paper_title: Lattice Thermal Conductivity of MgO and the MgSiO$_3$ Polymorphs Bridgmanite and Post-Perovskite at Lower-Mantle Conditions Using Fine-Tuned MACE Potentials
